sophie-ps: Heads-up — starting a pilot with OrionPay. Their infra exposes a single HTTP/2 tunnel and they're planning to multiplex a few hundred logical streams. Main asks: JS + Python mux snippets, curl fallback, consistent telemetry labels for their APM, ephemeral token rotation pattern, SOC2 questionnaire path, and a hosted vs dedicated cost ballpark for short 4k QPS spikes (2-5min bursts).

mark-sales: Demo Fri 11am PT. They will start on Hosted; may request Dedicated if jitter is high. Can we get a one-page runbook + quick code samples by Wed?

eli-runtime: Quick notes on muxing: our streaming endpoint supports logical streams identified by stream_id over a single transport. If their proxy supports websocket with subprotocols we do client-side mux; otherwise use the header-based mode for HTTP/2. JS example (minimal):
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, enableMux: true });
const a = client.stream({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', streamId: 'orion-req-1', trace: true });
a.on('data', d => console.log('a', d));
const b = client.stream({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', streamId: 'orion-req-2' });
// both logical streams reuse the same websocket/transport
```
If proxy rewrites the upgrade, set transportHint: 'http2-proxy' and include stream_id header. Fallback: open independent connections or use non-streaming / batch endpoints.

tara-devex: Python snippet for header-based muxing:
```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'), transport_hint='http2-proxy')
stream = client.stream(model='gpt-4o-mini', stream_id='orion-01', trace=True)
for chunk in stream:
    print('chunk', chunk)
# start another logical stream
stream2 = client.stream(model='gpt-4o-mini', stream_id='orion-02')
```
Curl fallback (non-streaming):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"Summarize this...","max_tokens":150}'
```

eli-runtime: Telemetry labels to set per logical stream: service=orionpay, env=pilot, stream_id, tenant, demo_id. Set trace:true to emit traces into our console and forward x-trace-id to their APM for correlation.

tara-devex: For structured output/tool-calling, small contract for demo so they can validate quickly:
```json
{"name":"normalize_payment","params":{"type":"object","properties":{"payer":{"type":"string"},"amount_cents":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["amount_cents"]}}
```
Recommend they run 5-10 validation prompts locally and share the results with Optimize before demo.

sec-guild-bot: Compliance: please have their procurement send the vendor SOC2 questionnaire PDF to security@redwood.ai. Quick blockers we need to triage: (1) data flow diagram showing what crosses our endpoints, (2) retention policy & whether raw utterances contain PII, (3) KMS/HSM details if they request Dedicated. Typical turnaround 2-4 business days after receipt of docs.

mark-sales: Pricing ask: bursts ~4k QPS for 2-5 minutes, maybe 3-4 times/day. Any ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated?

eli-runtime: For that pattern options: (A) Hosted with negotiated burst credits — common for pilots; (B) short-term Dedicated slice sized for the peak. Ballpark Dedicated slice to handle those peaks: $10k-20k/mo depending on GPU family & quantization. Hosted burst credit pricing is usually handled case-by-case; for the demo we can offer a simulated 1k QPS 5-min run and collect perf metrics.

tara-devex: Operational checklist for the demo (short):
- Provision ephemeral demo API key scoped to a demo workspace (rotate every 10-15m)
- Share expected payload size and max_token length so we can tune batching/window_ms
- Enable enableMux/transportHint and set trace:true for demos
- Provide SP metadata if they want SAML SSO in the pilot (test user needed)
- Provide short validation set (5 prompts) for structured output checks

sophie-ps: Can someone assemble the 1-page runbook + JS/Python snippets + curl fallback by EOD Wed? I'll share procurement contact and the questionnaire when I get it.

eli-runtime: I can draft the runbook and include a tiny python load simulator + kernel tuning notes (max_tokens, batch_window_ms).

tara-devex: I'll add troubleshooting notes: common mux failures (header stripping, connection coalescing), token expiry 401 handling (refresh dance), and quick parsing debug for function calls.

mark-sales: I'll write a one-paragraph pricing note and an optional offer: temporary reserved slice for demo week at a discounted pilot rate.

sec-guild-bot: Confirmed — security will triage SOC2 once questionnaire + dataflow diagram arrive.

sophie-ps: Scheduling: 30m sync Thu 9am PT to finalize runbook and pricing? :calendar:

eli-runtime: Works for me. :thumbsup:

tara-devex: Works. I'll drop a calendar invite and attach the first draft runbook when ready.

mark-sales: I'll join with pricing slide and sample contract language.

sophie-ps: Thanks team — sending initial payload examples and QPS histogram to the channel now. :rocket:
